verdict.rationale: The REST API clearly exposes tax-posture data and actions an agent could use — nexus list, registrations, filings, exemptions endpoints — and API keys support expiration and multi-key rotation (kintsugi-docs-11,12,13,14,24,5,17). However, the documented MCP server is explicitly scoped to serving API documentation/OpenAPI spec to coding assistants for writing integration code, not to reading or acting on a customer's actual tax posture (kintsugi-docs-6, kintsugi-docs-18); no evidence shows an MCP tool that queries nexus/registrations/filings or scoped read/write credential tiers beyond simple key expiry. Missing for 10: an MCP surface (or any agent-facing surface) that actually reads/acts on live nexus, registration, liability, or filing data, and evidence of fine-grained scoped permissions (e.g., read-only vs. filing-write) rather than just key expiration.
